jobs.title: Principle Software Engineer (Remote, United Kingdom)
jobs.description:
Job Summary:

JOB DESCRIPTION – Principal Engineer

Location: Remote, United Kingdom

Division: Ticketmaster

Contract Terms: Permanent

THE TEAM

The TM1 Maps team builds and operates the B2B application used to create and manage maps for the Ticketmaster website. The platform supports the full map request workflow, from submission through review and approval, and provides the tooling that produces map data during event build.

As part of this team, you will work on a product with direct impact on how live events are represented and prepared for fans, clients, and internal teams. The team owns the full lifecycle of its services, including architecture, delivery, testing, reliability, and production support.

THE JOB

In the role of Principal Engineer, you will be responsible for shaping the architecture, quality, reliability, and modernization of the Maps platform. You will design and deliver scalable application components, lead complex technical work across the team, and help evolve legacy systems toward simpler, more maintainable integration patterns.

This is an individual contributor role with strong cross-team influence. You will work closely with Product, UX, engineering peers, and external integrating teams to turn product goals into robust technical solutions. You will mentor engineers, raise engineering standards, anticipate technical risks, and help the team deliver high-quality software with confidence. You will work hands-on with a large variety of technologies and will be part of an DevOps & Agile team, responsible for the full end to end delivery of new functionalities.

WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING

  • Lead the technical design and delivery of scalable, maintainable application components across the TM1 Maps platform.
  • Shape the architecture of the Maps application, with a focus on reliability, simplicity, observability, and long-term maintainability.
  • Partner with Product Managers, UX, and engineering teams to translate product goals into well-scoped technical plans.
  • Build and improve micro-frontends and backend services using React, TypeScript, Java, and Spring Boot.
  • Develop and operate services on AWS and Kubernetes.
  • Design and support shared services, APIs, and integrations used by internal and external teams.
  • Promote high-quality engineering practices, including automated testing, CI/CD, monitoring, alerting, performance tuning, and recovery automation.
  • Mentor engineers through technical guidance, design feedback, and practical coaching.
  • Build alignment across teams, resolve technical roadblocks, and help create shared understanding around architecture decisions.
  • Troubleshoot complex production issues and help improve the reliability and performance of real-time, end-to-end systems.
  • Participate in the on-call support rotation for systems owned by the team.

WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW (or TECHNICAL SKILLS)

Required Qualifications

  • Strong professional experience building and operating production software systems.
  • Strong Java development skills, including experience with Spring Boot.
  • Strong frontend development experience with React, JavaScript, and TypeScript.
  • Experience with NodeJS and Express
  • Experience designing shared services, APIs, and distributed applications.
  • Experience with microservices or event-driven architecture.
  • Experience applying software design patterns, SOLID principles, and maintainable engineering practices.
  • Experience improving, modernizing, and supporting legacy systems.
  • Experience with production reliability, monitoring, alerting, troubleshooting, and performance improvement.
  • Experience with CI/CD and delivery tooling such as Maven, GitLab CI, or similar.
  • Working knowledge of one or more database technologies, such as DynamoDB, Oracle, MySQL, or MongoDB.
  • Experience working in Agile and DevOps-oriented teams with responsibility for delivery and production support.
  • Ability to influence technical direction across teams without relying on direct people-management authority.

Preferred qualifications

  • Working knowledge of Elasticsearch.
  • Working knowledge of Kafka.
  • Experience building or operating services on AWS.
  • Experience deploying or supporting applications on Kubernetes.
  • Experience supporting teams that integrate with shared platforms or services.

YOU (BEHAVIOURAL SKILLS)

  • You are autonomous, proactive, and comfortable leading technical work with minimal supervision.
  • You communicate clearly with engineers, product partners, UX, and remote teammates.
  • You enjoy mentoring engineers and helping teams raise their technical standards.
  • You are pragmatic about modernization, balancing long-term architecture goals with delivery needs.
  • You build strong working relationships across teams and help create alignment where priorities or constraints differ.
  • You are motivated by reliability, simplicity, and continuous improvement.
  • You are comfortable working in cross-functional and multidisciplinary teams.

LIFE AT TICKETMASTER

We are proud to be a part of Live Nation Entertainment, the world’s largest live entertainment company.

Our vision at Ticketmaster is to connect people around the world to the live events they love. As the world’s largest ticket marketplace and the leading global provider of enterprise tools and services for the live entertainment business, we are uniquely positioned to successfully deliver on that vision.

We do it all with an intense passion for Live and an inspiring and diverse culture driven by accessible leaders, attentive managers, and enthusiastic teams. If you’re passionate about live entertainment like we are, and you want to work at a company dedicated to helping millions of fans experience it, we want to hear from you.

Our work is guided by our values:

Reliability - We understand that fans and clients rely on us to power their live event experiences, and we rely on each other to make it happen.

Teamwork - We believe individual achievement pales in comparison to the level of success that can be achieved by a team

Integrity - We are committed to the highest moral and ethical standards on behalf of the countless partners and stakeholders we represent

Belonging - We are committed to building a culture in which all people can be their authentic selves, have an equal voice and opportunities to thrive

EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES

We are passionate and committed to our people and go beyond the rhetoric of diversity and inclusion. You will be working in an inclusive environment and be encouraged to bring your whole self to work. We will do all that we can to help you successfully balance your work and homelife. As a growing business we will encourage you to develop your professional and personal aspirations, enjoy new experiences, and learn from the talented people you will be working with. It's talent that matters to us and we encourage applications from people irrespective of their gender, race, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability status or caring responsibilities.

HIRING PRACTICES

The preceding job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job.

Ticketmaster recruitment policies are designed to place the most highly qualified persons available in a timely and efficient manner. Ticketmaster may pursue all avenues available, including promotion from within, employee referrals, outside advertising, employment agencies, internet recruiting, job fairs, college recruiting and search firms. Ticketmaster may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support application screening and assessment. All hiring decisions are made with human review.

Live Nation Entertainment will never request payment or equipment purchases as part of the hiring process. Recruiters will only contact candidates from official Live Nation or affiliated brand email domains.

jobs.title: Study Start-Up Lead
jobs.description:
The Study Start Up (SSU) team provides successful end to end coordination of Study Start-Up planning and execution activities including, but not limited to, investigator assessment and identification, pre-study development, site qualification, and site activation. SSU is a pivotal role requiring collaboration with internal and external stakeholders, working closely with the clinical study team, other internal functional areas, and Sponsors to support the study start-up process.

What You’ll Be Doing:

Project Oversight & Support

  • Leads and manages regional SSU efforts and develop Start-Up plans for country and site activation on studies of moderate scope and complexity
  • Participates in Sponsor meetings with respect to study start-up, including endorsement of the SSU operational targets & mitigation of delivery risks, establishing client expectations for delivery, communication, reporting, and metrics with oversight from a higher level SSU Lead when necessary
  • Partners closely with both Functional Leads and SSU team members to proactively identify and resolve study start up related issues

Feasibility & Site Identification

  • Oversees country and site feasibility activities, ensuring timely collection and evaluation of site capabilities, Regulatory & IRB/IEC considerations, and study-specific requirements; reviews / interprets site feasibility data to identify risks or barriers to site selection and activation
  • Coordinates with internal teams to confirm site recommendations and ensure alignment with study strategy

Regulatory & IRB/IEC Submissions & Approvals

  • Drives the regional Regulatory and IRB/IEC submission and approval strategy and manages country-level Regulatory and IRB/IEC submission and approval timelines
  • Participates in and coordinates country-level Regulatory and IRB/IEC submission preparation and approval activities, ensuring compliance with regional requirements
  • Coordinates cross-functional input (Regulatory, Medical, Legal, Clinical Operations) to prepare complete and accurate Regulatory and IRB/IEC submission packages

Site Essential Documents (SED) & ICF

  • Coordinate Informed Consent Form (ICF) development, country adaptation, review, negotiation, and approval with senior SSU support as needed.
  • Manage Site Essential Document (SED) requirements, templates, collection, review, approval, and second-level quality checks.

Budget & Contracts

  • Drives site budgets and contract negotiations, gains approval from Sponsor and Rho Legal, and files completed documents
  • Collaborates with applicable departments, Client, and stakeholders for obtaining site budget and contract templates and negotiation tools/trackers
  • Provides updates to Sponsor and internal team regarding negotiation progress and anticipated timelines

Systems, Metrics & Handoffs

  • Ensures that relevant SSU systems are maintained and up to date to analyze study start up progress metrics against targets/timelines
  • Ensures accurate documentation and timely handoffs to sponsor and internal project team

Stakeholder Engagement & Communication

Role overview

We're looking for an experienced personal finance writer with strong knowledge of the financial landscape across Russia and excellent writing and editorial skills in Russian.

You'll help create, review, and maintain accurate, engaging, and accessible personal finance content for nudge, covering everything from everyday money management and budgeting to investing, retirement, and other financial topics relevant to the local market.

This role combines personal finance expertise, strong writing and editorial skills, and the effective use of AI-assisted tools. You'll be responsible for creating clear, accurate, and engaging personal finance content that helps people understand their options and make informed financial decisions. AI-assisted tools support research, editing, and quality assurance, while human judgement, accuracy, and editorial ownership remain central to everything we produce.

Responsibilities

  • Act as nudge's personal finance subject-matter expert for Russia, maintaining a strong understanding of local financial products, regulations, government initiatives, and developments affecting consumers

  • Research, pitch, write, and refine personal finance content, including evergreen articles, educational posts, and other formats

  • Use AI-assisted tools to support research, editing, and quality assurance while maintaining full editorial responsibility for the content

  • Critically evaluate suggestions and feedback from AI-assisted editorial tools, applying independent judgement to determine appropriate changes

  • Participate in human-in-the-loop (HITL) editorial workflows, reviewing feedback, resolving identified issues, and ensuring content meets nudge's quality standards

  • Independently verify financial information using reliable and authoritative sources

  • Review and update existing content to reflect changes in legislation, financial products, and local market developments

  • Adapt complex financial topics into clear, practical, and engaging content appropriate for the intended audience, while following nudge's editorial guidelines and tone of voice

  • Identify relevant and timely content opportunities, proposing ideas based on market developments, audience needs, and content priorities

  • Collaborate with regional content managers and other internal stakeholders to meet deadlines and maintain consistent editorial standards

Skills and experience

  • Have strong knowledge of personal finance across Russia, including relevant financial regulations, consumer financial products, and government schemes

  • Demonstrate excellent writing, editing, and proofreading skills in Russian, with the ability to explain complex financial information clearly and naturally

  • Have experience creating clear, accurate, and engaging personal finance content that makes complex financial topics accessible to different audiences

  • Be comfortable using AI-assisted tools within an editorial workflow, with an understanding of their strengths and limitations

  • Demonstrate strong editorial judgement and the ability to critically evaluate automated suggestions rather than accepting them without question

  • Understand the importance of human oversight, factual accuracy, and accountability when using AI-assisted tools

  • Be adaptable and willing to learn new technologies and editorial processes

  • Have strong attention to detail, particularly when reviewing financial figures, regulatory requirements, eligibility conditions, and other potentially sensitive information

  • Be able to write and edit naturally in Russian, ensuring that content is locally relevant and does not read like a literal translation or unedited AI output

  • Have strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the confidence and professionalism to represent nudge in client-facing discussions when required

  • Be organised, reliable, and able to manage deadlines while working independently in a remote, collaborative environment

  • Be adaptable and open to evolving tools, technologies, and editorial processes

Experience with AI-assisted editorial processes, localisation, personal finance content, or multilingual editorial workflows would be an advantage.

The Solutions Architect turns business needs into sound technical solutions. You will work with business leaders, project managers, vendor architects and subject-matter experts to identify needs, plan delivery alongside other initiatives, and make sure solutions are secure, scalable and maintainable.

Our products run as hosted cloud services and as on-premises installs at customer sites, so the role needs strong judgement across cloud, hybrid and on-premises designs.

Solution design and delivery

  • Take part in technical change control: changes are risk-rated, test requirements are defined, and costs and impacts are quantified.

Standards and technical leadership

  • Working knowledge of application security best practices and tools for web, mobile and cloud applications.
  • Experience authoring architecture standards, guidelines and process documentation at system and enterprise level.
  • Ability to evaluate options on cost, risk and benefit, negotiate trade-offs between features and scalability, and drive decisions with multiple stakeholders.

Preferred qualifications

  • Real production exposure to high-availability issues, such as clustering.

jobs.description:
Product Manager — Virtualisation & Cloud Infrastructure

Location: Remote in Europe / EMEA

Department: Product Management

Employment type: Contractor friendly

Virtuozzo is a provider of infrastructure software for AI and the cloud, helping cloud service providers, SaaS companies, and enterprises build and operate efficient, scalable infrastructure. We combine an optimized operating system with orchestration, management, automation, and protection to deliver mainframe-like efficiency, performance, reliability, versatility, and security—while reducing overall cost and complexity.

Our Virtuozzo Infrastructure System (V/IS) brings together compute, storage, and networking to support traditional applications, cloud-native workloads, and AI services. We help organisations modernise their infrastructure, make better use of their hardware, and bring new cloud- and GPU-powered services to market on their own infrastructure and under their own brand.

Our technology serves more than 100,000 companies in over 100 countries. With deep engineering roots, we pioneered container-based virtualisation and continue to contribute to foundational open-source projects, including OpenVZ, the Linux kernel, Kubernetes, CRIU, KVM, and OpenStack.

The Role:

We are looking for a Product Manager for V/IS to help shape the future of the Virtuozzo product suite, including virtualisation, cloud management platforms, and infrastructure solutions for CSP, MSP, and SME markets.

This is a high-impact role for someone who combines strong product judgement, technical depth, market awareness, and customer empathy. You will work closely with engineering, sales, marketing, support, and customer-facing teams to define what we build, why we build it, how we position it, and how it creates measurable value for customers.

This is not a pure backlog-management role. We are looking for someone who can think strategically, engage deeply with technical customers, understand infrastructure markets, make clear prioritisation decisions, and turn product direction into execution.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Drive product strategy for the Virtuozzo product suite, including virtualisation, cloud management platforms, and infrastructure solutions for CSP, MSP, and SME markets.
  • Develop a comprehensive product roadmap that aligns with company business objectives, customer needs, market opportunities, and Virtuozzo’s broader platform direction.
  • Engage with key customers and stakeholders to gather insights, validate product hypotheses, and refine strategies to address market demands.
  • Collaborate closely with engineering, marketing, sales, and support teams to ensure successful execution of product launches, feature iterations, and market positioning.
  • Lead market analysis to identify trends, opportunities, and competitive threats, ensuring Virtuozzo is positioned to capitalise on new technologies and shifts in the market.
  • Define and implement pricing models and value propositions that drive customer adoption and revenue growth while maintaining a competitive edge in the market.
  • Work on cross-product initiatives to create a seamless experience across the Virtuozzo ecosystem, including integrations with third-party tools and emerging technologies.
  • You will also help connect product strategy to real customer outcomes: faster cloud service launches, lower infrastructure cost, better operational efficiency, improved monetisation for service providers, and a simpler experience across the Virtuozzo platform.

What You Bring

  • 5+ years of product management experience in cloud infrastructure, virtualisation, cloud management platforms, infrastructure software, hosting, telco cloud, MSP/CSP platforms, or adjacent technical domains.
  • Strong understanding of cloud infrastructure technologies such as virtualisation, KVM, OpenStack, Kubernetes, software-defined storage, networking, orchestration, automation, or cloud management platforms.
  • Experience building product strategy and roadmaps for technical B2B products used by infrastructure teams, service providers, managed service providers, enterprises, or SaaS companies.
  • Ability to work closely with engineering teams and engage in technical discussions with architects, developers, solution architects, support engineers, and customer operations teams.
  • Strong customer-discovery skills, with the ability to translate technical and commercial pain points into clear product priorities.
  • Experience with market analysis, competitor research, pricing, packaging, value propositions, and product positioning.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create clear product narratives, roadmap updates, business cases, and launch materials.
  • A structured, analytical approach to prioritization, with comfort using customer input, market data, usage data, commercial impact, and technical feasibility to make product decisions.
  • Confidence working across distributed, international teams.

Nice to Have

  • CSP, MSP, hosting, telco, or cloud service provider environments.
  • VMware alternatives, OpenStack-based platforms, KVM-based virtualisation, Kubernetes orchestration, or infrastructure automation.
  • Product ownership for cloud control panels, cloud management platforms, portals, billing integrations, self-service platforms, or infrastructure operations tooling.
  • Pricing and packaging for infrastructure software, subscription models, usage-based models, or service-provider commercial models.
  • Familiarity with AI infrastructure, GPU infrastructure, edge infrastructure, hybrid cloud, or multi-cloud management.

What We Offer

  • Remote work from Europe / EMEA.
  • Flexible working hours and a distributed international team.
  • High ownership and visibility within the Product organisation.
  • The opportunity to influence product and R&D direction from day one.
  • A technical, engineering-driven culture with practical decision-making and minimal bureaucracy.
  • Work on meaningful infrastructure products used by cloud providers, MSPs, SaaS companies, and enterprises.
  • Private medical insurance support, depending on location and employment setup.
  • Additional benefits depending on country, location, and preferred employment method.

jobs.title: Director, Member Lifecycle and Personalization
jobs.description:
Job Description

A bit about this role:


Devoted grew from 212,000 members in December 2025 to more than half a million in September 2026. In 2027, we’ll serve Medicare beneficiaries across 34 states and 1,341 counties. Our engagement work already gets results: new-member digital engagement is up 30% year over year. Our next opportunity is precision—knowing each member well enough to reach them at the right moment, on the right channel, or to not contact them at all.


You’ll own member retention for members across AEP, members at risk of leaving, and preventing involuntary loss. You’ll also build the shared capabilities that every engagement journey runs on: experimentation, decisioning, and contact governance across SMS, email, push, in-app, mail, and outbound phone. The leaders who own onboarding, clinical engagement, and MyDevoted are your partners, and they should move faster because of what you build.


This is a player-coach role. In your first quarter, you’ll write the first experiment plan, build a journey, and draft the first cross-journey contact policy. You’ll lead our engagement operations team. You’ll add the capabilities it needs next and move our work from hand-built programs to a system that composes, tests, and learns.


Engagement runs on Devoted’s own technology platform, the same one behind our growth, so you’ll have control over data, decisioning, and the member experience that off-the-shelf tools can’t offer. The journeys and channels are built. We need the leader who builds the intelligence that decides what each member needs next.


You’ll report to the Chief Experience Officer.


Responsibilities will include:

  • Testing, learning, and measurement strategy. You’ll assess where our testing, targeting, and decisioning capabilities stand today and set the plan to close the gaps. Then you’ll raise how many tests we run and how fast we act on them. That means holdouts across every channel; a decision rule set before each launch; and a clear recommendation on what scales, what changes, and what stops. You’ll keep a learning agenda that works with slow, noisy health outcomes and a once-a-year enrollment cycle.
  • Plan-year lifecycle (retention and renewal). You’ll own the member journey around the plan year. You’ll partner with our insights team so disenrollment learnings feed directly into our annual benefit design process.
  • Contact governance. You’ll build one view of every message a member receives and turn it into a user-centered, data-informed policy that systems enforce: frequency limits, suppression, quiet hours, and channel preferences across the health plan and medical group. You’ll do this in partnership with Legal, Compliance, and clinical leaders.
  • Decisioning. You’ll weigh each member’s competing needs (clinical, retention, and service) to decide what to send, on which channel, and when to send nothing. You’ll start with rules and add models where they earn their place.
  • Composable content. Work with content team to operationalize hand-built campaigns into a small set of durable pieces that can be combined and tested across more than 700 plan variations.
  • Team leadership and operations. You’ll lead our engagement operations and content team and own the reliability, compliance, and quality of everything it ships. You’ll develop its leaders, hire for what we need next, and set the operating rhythm as the work shifts from hand-built to system-driven.

Required skills and experience:

  • You’ve built experimentation or personalization programs for consumers.
  • You’ve owned a consumer metric end to end and moved it.
  • You’ve built and grown a team, including hiring leaders.
  • You’re a player-coach. You can design an experiment and defend its statistics, challenge an engineering estimate, and rewrite a message yourself.
  • You’ve used emerging technology to materially improve engagement work, and you have good judgment and curiosity/experience about AI evaluation, human oversight, and where deterministic rules work better than models.
  • You have 10+ years of experience, including leading leaders.

Desired skills and experience:

  • Consumer subscription, fintech, consumer health, or marketplace businesses where retention is the business model
  • Healthcare, insurance, financial services, or other regulated, trust-dependent environments
  • Experience on either side of engagement platforms: running lifecycle or CRM programs on them, or building them


Salary range: $182,000 - $278,000 / year

The pay range listed for this position is the range the organization reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for this position at the time of the posting. Once the interview process begins, your talent partner will provide additional information on the compensation for the role, along with additional information on our total rewards package. The actual base salary offered will depend on a variety of factors, including the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, specific and unique skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job.

Our Total Rewards package includes:

  • Employer sponsored health, dental and vision plan with low or no premium

  • Generous paid time off

  • $100 monthly mobile or internet stipend

  • Stock options for all employees

  • Bonus eligibility for all roles excluding Director and above; Commission eligibility for Sales roles

  • Parental leave program

  • 401K program

  • And more....

*Our total rewards package is for full time employees only. Intern and Contract positions are not eligible.

Founded in 2017, Devoted Health is on a mission to dramatically improve the health and well-being of older Americans by caring for everyone like they are family, and that includes our employees. Our robust and seamlessly integrated care platform merges advanced data and AI access with world-class clinical and service experiences to create a member experience that is unlike the industry norm. To continue building upon our mission, we want to bring together those who share our values, embrace change and advancement, and are enthusiastic about where we're going — all the while bringing their own unique qualities, experiences, and expertise, in hopes of further changing the healthcare experience.


Devoted is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to a safe and supportive work environment in which all employees have the opportunity to participate and contribute to the success of the business. We value diversity and collaboration. Individuals are respected for their skills, experience, and unique perspectives. This commitment is embodied in Devoted’s Code of Conduct, our company values and the way we do business.


As an Equal Opportunity Employer, the Company does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy status, marital status, national origin, disability, age, sexual orientation, veteran status, genetic information, gender identity, gender expression, or any other factor prohibited by law. Pulmovant is a Roivant-backed clinical-stage biotechnology company committed to transforming the lives of patients with pulmonary diseases. Pulmovant’s first investigational candidate, mosliciguat, is designed to provide a novel, once-daily, inhaled treatment option for patients with pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD). Mosliciguat is a potential first-in-class soluble guanylate cyclase activator with a differentiated mechanism of action currently being evaluated in the Phase 3 PHrontier global clinical trial in PH-ILD, but with potential broad applicability across the PH and ILD disease landscape.

Pulmovant recently announced positive results from its Phase 2 PHocus study evaluating mosliciguat for the treatment of pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD), a progressive and life-threatening condition with significant unmet medical needs for patients. PHocus met both primary and secondary endpoints including the highest ever reported pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) reduction in any randomized controlled PH trial. The robust results, in conjunction with mosliciguat’s once-daily, inhaled administration and potential first-in-class sGC activator profile, strongly position it as a potential single agent treatment and combination therapy for patients with PH-ILD. These data represent a significant advancement in a devastating disease that affects ~200,000 patients with no or very limited treatment options. A Phase 3 trial is currently underway. More details can be found in the press release here.

As part of the Roivant family of companies, Pulmovant leverages the power of collaboration and innovation to drive progress.

jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for an AI Engineer, Merchant Copilots to build intelligent, reliable, and useful AI-powered assistants for Bask Health's merchant-facing platform.

Bask Health enables entrepreneurs and healthcare businesses to launch and operate direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses. Merchants use our platform to manage storefronts, configure products, monitor business activity, understand operational workflows, and coordinate the technology behind their businesses.

As the platform grows, we want to make these capabilities easier to access and use. You'll help build AI copilots that allow merchants to interact with platform information, understand complex workflows, and complete supported tasks through natural language and intelligent assistance.

This is a hands-on engineering role that combines large language models, backend development, tool calling, application integrations, and product engineering. You'll work with model APIs, retrieval systems, internal services, and structured business data to develop AI experiences that are deeply integrated into Bask's applications.

Your work may include conversational merchant assistants, AI-powered platform navigation, business information retrieval, configuration guidance, operational summaries, and automation for repetitive administrative tasks.

You'll collaborate with product managers, backend engineers, frontend engineers, and applied AI specialists to understand merchant needs and turn those needs into reliable software features. You'll contribute to technical design, develop production code, test AI behavior, and improve systems based on real user feedback.

Because merchant copilots may interact with business information and platform configuration, you'll need to design appropriate permissions, confirmation steps, and safeguards. AI assistants should help merchants complete authorized tasks without making unapproved changes or exposing information from other merchant accounts.

We're looking for an engineer who enjoys building useful AI products, understands how to connect language models to real application functionality, and can turn complex merchant workflows into intuitive software experiences.

What You'll Do

  • Design, build, and maintain AI-powered merchant copilots across Bask Health's platform.
  • Develop conversational assistants that help merchants navigate platform features and workflows.
  • Integrate large language models into merchant-facing applications and backend services.
  • Build AI capabilities that help merchants understand account settings, storefront configuration, and operational information.
  • Develop natural language interfaces for retrieving approved business and platform data.
  • Implement tool-calling systems that allow AI assistants to interact with authorized platform functionality.
  • Connect merchant copilots to internal APIs, services, and structured data sources.
  • Build retrieval-augmented generation pipelines for merchant documentation, help content, and platform knowledge.
  • Develop AI-assisted workflows for storefront setup, product configuration, and other merchant tasks.
  • Implement contextual assistance that responds to the merchant's current application state.
  • Build AI-generated summaries of approved operational and business information.
  • Develop structured output handling for AI-assisted application workflows.
  • Implement validation and confirmation steps before executing consequential platform actions.
  • Ensure merchant copilots respect account permissions, tenant isolation, and data access restrictions.
  • Design safeguards against unauthorized tool use, prompt injection, and unreliable AI outputs.
  • Collaborate with frontend engineers to create intuitive conversational and embedded AI interfaces.
  • Work with product managers to identify repetitive merchant tasks that could benefit from AI assistance.
  • Develop reusable components and backend services for merchant-facing AI applications.
  • Implement automated testing for model responses, tool execution, and application integrations.
  • Evaluate AI outputs for accuracy, relevance, completeness, and usefulness.
  • Investigate incorrect responses, failed tool calls, and unexpected assistant behavior.
  • Improve prompts, retrieval logic, and model configurations based on evaluation results.
  • Implement monitoring, logging, and tracing for AI-powered merchant features.
  • Optimize model usage, response latency, reliability, and operational costs.
  • Handle API failures, timeouts, retries, and fallback behavior.
  • Participate in code reviews, architecture discussions, and engineering planning.
  • Collaborate with senior engineers to establish reliable patterns for AI-assisted platform actions.
  • Own assigned merchant copilot features from implementation through deployment and ongoing improvement.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, preferably including applied AI or AI-powered application development.
  • Experience building and deploying production software applications.
  • Strong programming skills in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, or comparable languages.
  • Hands-on experience integrating large language models into software applications.
  • Familiarity with modern model APIs and generative AI development patterns.
  • Understanding of prompt engineering and structured model outputs.
  • Experience building backend services and application APIs.
  • Familiarity with tool calling, function calling, or AI-assisted application actions.
  • Experience integrating third-party services and internal APIs.
  • Understanding of authentication, authorization, and secure application design.
  • Familiarity with relational databases and structured application data.
  • Experience building reliable asynchronous workflows and service integrations.
  • Understanding of multi-tenant application architecture and data isolation.
  • Ability to translate business workflows into software functionality.
  • Experience writing maintainable, well-tested production code.
  • Familiarity with automated testing, debugging, and code review practices.
  • Understanding of the limitations and failure modes of large language models.
  • Ability to evaluate AI outputs and identify quality or reliability issues.
  • Familiarity with cloud-based application deployment.
  • Experience with logging, monitoring, and production troubleshooting.
  • Understanding of API error handling, retries, and fallback strategies.
  • Experience working with Git and collaborative software development workflows.
  • Ability to collaborate with product managers, designers, and other engineers.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to independently own assigned engineering projects from development through deployment.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building AI copilots, conversational assistants, or agent-powered applications.
  • Familiarity with OpenAI, Anthropic, or comparable model APIs.
  • Experience with AI agent frameworks and orchestration libraries.
  • Experience building applications that use LLM tool calling or function calling.
  • Familiarity with retrieval-augmented generation architectures.
  • Experience with embeddings, semantic search, and vector databases.
  • Experience developing natural language interfaces for business software.
  • Familiarity with AI-powered workflow automation and multi-step task execution.
  • Experience building merchant-facing SaaS products or e-commerce platforms.
  • Understanding of storefront management, product catalogs, subscriptions, or commerce operations.
  • Experience with multi-tenant SaaS application architecture.
  • Familiarity with TypeScript and Node.js backend development.
  • Experience with React or Next.js applications.
  • Familiarity with tRPC, Prisma, Drizzle, or comparable development tools.
  • Experience working with AWS or serverless application infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with AI evaluation frameworks and automated model testing.
  • Experience implementing human confirmation and approval workflows for AI actions.
  • Understanding of prompt injection risks and secure AI tool execution.
  • Experience building AI-powered analytics or business information retrieval features.
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor or Claude Code.

jobs.title: Google Ads Manager
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager (Remote - US CT/ET)
jobs.description:
High-level stuff you might be filtering against 🔍

Location: Remote (CT/ET Timezone). Collaborating with teams on the West Coast and in Europe.
Type: Full-time
Salary: Location dependent. As a guide, our current range across all levels is $160k-$190k. We are open to negotiation as we recognise there are different situations, but these are our general guardrails.

What I am looking for

👋 Hi, I’m Martin, Chief Technology Officer at Zen Educate and I’m looking for an Engineering Manager who can make an impact on the real-world problem of education staffing, and do it by leading a team in engineering excellence.
Every place has its own understanding of what engineering excellence looks like (sometimes written down, sometimes not). Here’s what it means to me and Zen:
  • Valuing real-world outcomes and shared learning over output
  • Product thinking over pure tech - start with the problem, ship quickly and iterate.
  • Team success and sustainability over individual heroics.
We are a small, but mighty team and so every person has the opportunity to make an outsized impact and put their stamp on what excellence looks like in practice. What do I mean by “small”? Today we have 21 Product Engineers, all reporting to one Senior Engineering Manager, working in small, dynamic teams across the Zen product.
We recognise the world is not static - “what got us here, won’t get us there” - so we look for curiosity, adaptability and proactiveness as fundamental traits. The leaders I see being most successful in Product and Tech are those who focus on identifying and solving problems, and then use technology to turn those solutions into scalable systems. We’re aiming for ‘antigravity’ - using automation to get faster and multiply impact as we scale.
This role is particularly exciting because you’ll be Zen’s first Engineering Manager in the US, where we’re enjoying rapid growth. You’ll thrive in this role if you’re someone who can build relationships quickly, take strong ownership of problems end-to-end and hire and grow a team around you 💪

What we are building and why

Getting the right teacher into the right school at the right time is a crucial problem to solve, both for education outcomes for children and for the sustainability of an industry that spends billions on this.
Today the platform we are building supports internal operations teams on filling roles, educators on finding roles via our mobile app and schools on getting educators in for both short-term and long-term roles. The more we develop the platform (and the ability to self-serve in the marketplace), the more efficient the whole process becomes, which means more money going back to educators and into classrooms (over $65 million globally since 2017).
We are well established in the UK and growing at a phenomenal rate in the US 🚀
What we need now is to reach the next level in how we scale the engineering team to support this growth. That’s where you come in 😉

What the role looks like in practice

I’ve written a bunch of words above that I hope capture your interest and excitement ✨. But what really matters is what reality looks like and the best person to share that is the person already doing the job. So here’s a glimpse of work over the last few weeks from Sean, our Senior Engineering Manager:

“I’ve been building a system to automate the admin of managing lots of engineers, so I can focus on the fun, human parts of my role - great conversations with great people! Those have included 1:1s with Product Engineers exploring when work flows well for them and how to make that happen more often, interviewing Mission Leads to gather feedback ahead of our upcoming performance cycle, and working with our People Lead to navigate a tricky situation and manage the impact on my team.

I’ve been partnering with the CTO to develop our compensation and levelling philosophy. Following our last pay review cycle some of our engineers were promoted up a level, and so Martin and I spent a day celebrating them in the Product and Tech Slack channel, with messages for each individual calling out the impact they’ve had in the last six months - a real privilege!

I’ve also organised time for the team to come together: a ‘How I Work’ session where engineers shared their cool AI-powered workflows, a training session on running an excellent demo, and a social to celebrate a departing team member. With the team growing, I’ve been hiring manager for 5 new Product Engineers and I’ve helped train members of the team to run our tech loops. And I’ve just shipped a small bugfix, to keep my hand in!”

The Engineering Manager role comes in many different shapes and sizes. At Zen, your primary focus will be people. You’ll be managing a large group of Product Engineers, but this isn’t a ‘people lead’ or ‘department head’ role: you’ll need to be close enough to your engineers and their work to help them grow, using tried-and-tested habits like excellent 1:1s and feedback to make this happen. In the background, you’ll spend time creating systems to automate processes, so you can invest your time in building relationships and increasing talent density in the team. As an Engineering Manager you can expect to be close to both the CTO and the CPO and their teams, and you’ll have the opportunity for huge influence and impact in Product and Tech.

What you might like or dislike

Every place makes tradeoffs based on what they value and where they are in their journey ⚖️. Here’s a list of things you might find useful in figuring out if this is the right role for you. If we end up chatting, feel free to dig deeper into any of them. Note that some of these are recent changes in our approach and may be “work in progress” when you join.

💻 How We Work

Missions, not org charts. Teams form around outcomes, not reporting lines, and process exists only where it serves performance. Your reports will be spread across several Missions at once, so you manage people and their growth, not a team or a backlog.
Wide scope and real leverage. Engineering Managers at Zen manage a large group of Product Engineers (typically 10-15 individuals). We’re growing fast, and you’ll be a Hiring Manager from early on, running interviews, debriefs and offers with our talent team. You’ll succeed through coaching, feedback and building relationships - always thinking about how to increase the talent density in the team. You won’t necessarily be the best engineer in the room, but you will contribute to technical conversations and decision making, and there will always be opportunities to ship a small improvement or bugfix!
High expectations and strong investment. Every engineer here has their own specific strengths and their own route to impact. You’ll help each person identify and build on what we often call their spikiness - those skills and behaviours they can leverage to do something special. You’ll do this through conversations and feedback, and through celebrating the work they do. At Zen we don’t have competency grids or performance frameworks: instead we focus on recognising examples of excellence - the real impact people have - which will look different for each person at each level. This means we also spot early when something isn’t working and have the honest conversations that follow. Sometimes that leads to hard decisions, and we’ll work through those together.
Experimenting to unlock new opportunities, tried-and-tested for the rest. There are lots of exciting ways to leverage systems and automation to increase the impact of a single manager across a large team. You’ll constantly be experimenting with AI and tooling to take on the admin and add value, but you’ll lean on proven habits, like great 1:1s and honest feedback, for the parts that benefit most from a human relationship.
Celebrate often. We make a point of marking wins, learnings and goodbyes, and as an Engineering Manager you’ll be someone people look to as a champion of that. This will mean celebrating when people get promoted to a new level, and giving them a great send-off when they choose to move on to new opportunities. It will also sometimes mean having awkward or challenging 1:1s about performance, and being a stable point as you navigate rapid change with your team.

🌱 Growth & Progression

Choose your own career path. We care most about impact and learning and we don’t have rigid competency grids. This means greater flexibility in what progression looks like, but requires you to build an understanding of what we value from guiding principles and shared real-world examples.
Few titles, infinite Levels. Roles at Zen define your scope, and Levels show your growth within it. As an Engineering Manager, your scope is the group of engineers you lead. Within that there’s no ceiling: you’ll move up Levels as your impact through your team grows, in how they develop, what they deliver, and how sustinable their work is.
Investment over reward as a mindset. Level changes are tightly coupled to compensation changes. Confidence in a Level change is based on sustainably doing great work at your current level. We think it is fairer to invest in what you do next, rather than reward you doing the next Level first for free!
Your manager is a partner, not a supervisor. You'll have a manager, but they won't be directing your every move. Expect them to help you think through hard problems, offer perspective, and provide nudges to help you grow - not to tell you what to do or check your work. That means you'll need to take ownership of your own progress and speak up when you need unblocking. We’ll look to you to be this kind of manager too, and to model these behaviours to others.

💸 Compensation

Market reality. Compensation is based on your competitiveness in your local hiring market (note that’s not just where you live). We don’t believe anyone has found a great solution to global compensation, so we aim instead to be clear and equitable in how we do it.
Solid, but not flashy compensation. We pay decently, but we won’t beat out companies with deeper pockets (yet!).
Think long-term investment. If you are in a place where you need to prioritise immediate financial gain then this probably isn’t the right time to join us.

🤝 Team Culture & Collaboration

Distributed engineering team. Solid communication skills and async habits are key to being effective. You’ll find strong connection here, but not through engineering getting together in-person. As an Engineering Manager, that means building strong trust and connection with 10-15 people you’ll mostly work with remotely. If you like the buzz of working near others you are welcome to work from one of our offices, but there won’t be many members of the engineering team there on any given day.
We believe in impact and measurable outcomes, alongside shared learning. If your work moves the needle or teaches us something meaningful then that’s a win. If not, then we’ll want to understand why.
Balanced, sustainable work. Long hours are not a badge of honour - they are an indication something isn’t working well. We value a sustainable pace and healthy teams, and as an Engineering Manager you’ll be one of the people making that real.
Diversity is good in some ways and lacking in others. You might be the first of something here. That matters and we’ll support appropriately if you are.

How we hire

Hire fast, fix fast. Hiring today is...not great, with most companies being too cautious and taking too long to make a decision 😦. We move quicker - our ideal is: apply Monday, offer by Friday. Then we invest heavily in the most important part - your onboarding. We ensure you are set up for success, with clear direction, quality time with each of your engineers, and exposure to the Missions they’re working on.
Whilst fast doesn’t mean frivolous, it does slightly increase the risk that you or we made a mistake. So we include regular check-ins during onboarding to make sure expectations match reality. If either side feels something is off then we try to fix it fast. And sometimes that will mean saying “let’s not carry on” with respect.
Real talk. We believe in being direct and authentic. We’ll share the good, the messy and the challenges. We recognise we won’t have all the answers, still have much to learn, and that’s all part of the fun of this wild ride 🚀. We expect the same from you - after all we are just a bunch of humans trying to do great work together.
Mindset, not tools. We hire for how you think and create leverage, not what specific tools you’ve used before. To us, experience is just another tool - it is only valuable through how you leverage it. Curiosity, adaptability, good judgement - those are the durable qualities in a changing world. And we value different opinions, so ensure you share yours - have a point of view, maybe debate a little and we will respect that.
Always open to great people. We are always hiring and happy to chat even if the timing isn’t quite right. That’s why you might see this job post open for a long time. We are not collecting resumes or doing stealth market research, we just believe in the power of serendipity. To make that more transparent - right now we have a clear need for 1 Engineering Manager in the team, but this is likely to grow in 2027.

Okay, so what will the actual process look like? 👀

Recruiter quick chat. Our recruiter will check you are human, can communicate effectively and cover some of the basics like compensation, benefits and availability.
Expertise. This will be with Sean, our Senior Engineering Manager. You’ll work through a real problem together that Sean’s faced in the past, and explore the different opportunities, decisions and tradeoffs you might encounter. He’ll be wanting to understand how you think about managing and growing people and get a sense of how you might work together.
Role chat. This will be with me. I’ll be wanting to understand how you think and approach the role and engineering excellence. I’ll start by asking you the question you include in your application. And I’ll want to dig into your answers so that this becomes more of a conversation and shared exploration than a Q&A session 😃.
Meet the team. This will be with members of the Product and Tech team - a PM or Designer and one or two Product Engineers - and it’s your chance to ask questions and build a picture of what it’s like to work at Zen. We’ll ask you to formulate these questions in advance and share them with us, to make the most of the time together.
Once interviewers have shared their feedback from each session we do an internal debrief - that’s where we discuss what we are excited about you for in the role, any challenges we see and whether we think we can mitigate them at this time. From there we will make a decision and either proceed to offer or tell you that we’re not offering.
We believe feedback is important, but also know not everyone wants it - so we don’t share it by default. If you’d like feedback after the process, just let us know. Note that we’ll frame the feedback from our perspective of why we did or did not have the confidence rather than as a commentary on you.

Interested? Let’s go!

If you read all of the above and are excited (maybe even a little nervous) about the opportunity and how we work then I recommend applying now! If you skipped or skimmed the above, feel free to apply anyway but you’re missing a bunch of useful information that could streamline the process for you 😉

jobs.title: Account Executive, GPU Infrastructure Sales
jobs.description:
Alpha Compute is at the cutting edge of high-performance computing, delivering specialized

GPU-as-a-Service (GPUaaS) infrastructure to the world's leading AI enterprises, foundational

model builders, and research institutions. Built on top-tier, high-density data center

environments and the latest NVIDIA architectures, we build and scale the critical underlying

infrastructure that powers the next generation of AI.

Within Alpha Compute's Global Infrastructure Business, we are seeking a relentless, proactive Account Executive to drive our growth strategy. This role is built for an ambitious sales professional who wants to embed themselves in the booming AI ecosystem, identifying and capturing new business opportunities within AI hardware infrastructure (GPUs, networking, and storage).

As an Account Executive, you will be on the front lines of the AI revolution. You will be responsible for full-cycle sales and strategic business development—working directly with customers, compute brokers, and tier-one/two suppliers to position Alpha Compute's GPUaaS offerings.

You will target rising AI startups, mid-market tech companies, and specialized research labs that require high-performance NVIDIA hardware. Under the mentorship of our executive sales leadership, you will create measurable customer value, lead RFP/RFI responses, and drive key metrics for revenue growth, operating profit, and market share.

Key Responsibilities

  • Strategic Business Development: Identify, qualify, and secure net-new business opportunities. Initiate, maintain, and grow influential client relationships while ensuring continuous lead generation in liaison with brokers and direct customers.
  • Full-Cycle Pipeline Management: Manage the entire sales cycle from lead generation to contract award. Keep your CRM (HubSpot) spotless and run a tight, predictable sales process.
  • Proposal & RFP Development: Lead and contribute to the development of compelling proposals, bids, and responses to Requests for Information (RFIs) and Requests for Proposals (RFPs).
  • Cost-Benefit & Technical Sales: Research and present detailed reports showing potential customers the financial and operational benefits of our GPUaaS solutions. Effectively articulate technical advantages to both engineering leads and procurement officers.

jobs.title: Sales Engineer - Spain
jobs.description:
Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) accelerates digital transformation so customers can be more agile, efficient, resilient, and secure. The Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange platform protects thousands of customers from cyberattacks and data loss by securely connecting users, devices, and applications in any location. Distributed across 200+ public data centers globally and thousands of private sites at the edge, the SASE-based Zero Trust Exchange is the world’s largest in-line cloud security platform.

We believe the future of work is Human + AI and are building an AI-native enterprise where human potential is amplified by machine intelligence to solve the world’s hardest security challenges. Driven by deep customer obsession, we are committed to the mission, outcome, and to each other. We bring these commitments to life through three core behaviors: ownership and collaboration, trust through outcomes and impact, and a challenge culture with ongoing feedback. Ready to make an impact at the company pioneering security transformation in the AI era? Join us at Zscaler.

About the Role
We are looking for a Sales Engineer to join our team. This is a remote role based out of Madrid, Spain, reporting to the Senior Sales Engineering Manager in the Solutions Consulting department. In this role, you will serve as the technical pivot point for our sales process, presenting the Zscaler cloud security platform to prospective customers and translating their business goals into enticing, high-impact recommendations. As a trusted advisor, you will guide clients through their digital transformation journeys, gathering technical requirements and driving proof-of-concept engagements, presentations, and custom demonstrations that clearly articulate our value proposition while collaborating closely with Account Executives and cross-functional teams to shape comprehensive account strategies.

What you’ll do (Role Expectations)

  • Present the Zscaler cloud security platform to prospective customers to demonstrate clear business value
  • Set the technical vision and translate customer goals into enticing, relevant recommendations
  • Act as a trusted advisor to clients, guiding and aiding them through their transformational security journey
  • Gather customer technical requirements and promote the value proposition through presentations, demonstrations, and proof-of-concept engagements
  • Partner closely with Account Executives, cross-functional specialists, and extended teams to shape strategic account plans

Who You Are (Success Profile)

  • You thrive in ambiguity. You're comfortable building the path as you walk it. You thrive in a dynamic environment, seeing ambiguity not as a hindrance, but as the raw material to build something meaningful.
  • You act like an owner. Your passion for the mission fuels your bias for action. You operate with integrity because you genuinely care about the outcome. True ownership involves leveraging dynamic range: the ability to navigate seamlessly between high-level strategy and hands-on execution.
  • You are a problem-solver. You love running towards the challenges because you are laser-focused on finding the solution, knowing that solving the hard problems delivers the biggest impact.
  • You are a high-trust collaborator. You are ambitious for the team, not just yourself. You embrace our challenge culture by giving and receiving ongoing feedback—knowing that candor delivered with clarity and respect is the truest form of teamwork and the fastest way to earn trust.
  • You are a learner. You have a true growth mindset and are obsessed with your own development, actively seeking feedback to become a better partner and a stronger teammate. You love what you do and you do it with purpose.

What We’re Looking for (Minimum Qualifications)

  • 5+ years of experience as a Sales Engineer or Systems Integrator
  • Deep knowledge of enterprise network or cloud security technologies
  • Proven experience working with Value Selling Methodologies
  • Demonstrated ability to produce high-impact presentations, technical demonstrations, and partner with sales teams to deliver proof-of-concept engagements
  • Foundational understanding of AI/ML technologies and experience leveraging, securing, or positioning AI-driven solutions to optimize outcomes within your functional domain
  • Fluent proficiency in Spanish is required for this role

What Will Make You Stand Out (Preferred Qualifications)

jobs.title: Senior Solutions Engineer | Switzerland | Remote
jobs.description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

The Opportunity

The Solutions Engineering team are the customer facing product experts. The team enables Grafana Labs worldwide growth by educating potential and existing customers to ensure that they are happy and successful. We share our technical and product expertise with customers through demos, hands on enablement, presentations, technical evaluations and ongoing interaction. We partner closely with our Sales team to help qualify and close opportunities. The Solutions Engineering team is one of the primary routes of communication from our customers to the Product Management and Engineering teams.

A Solutions Engineer is able to really listen to a prospect or customer, understand their requirements, ask the right questions to extract as much information as required and translate all that into a solution with Grafana Labs technology. They are the bridge between the highly technical engineering folks here at Grafana Labs, our customers and our Sales team.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Partnering with our Sales team to articulate the overall Grafana value proposition, vision and strategy to customers
  • Owning the technical engagement with customers and help close complex opportunities through advanced competitive knowledge, technical skill and credibility
  • Delivering product and technical presentations to potential and existing customers
  • Effectively communicate with customers and internal teams to provide feedback on our products and the competitive landscape
  • Driving product conversations based on need and problems with customers
  • Working with the team to enhance documentation, write blog posts, record videos, contribute knowledge base articles and create other public or private enablement material

What Makes you a Great Fit:

  • 5+ years of technical pre-sales experience
  • Be open to various and complex assignments, this will require strong judgment, collaboration, and leadership
  • You will need first class written and oral communication skills to collaborate with our remote-first internal teams and with our worldwide customers. You will need to be able to skillfully articulate our value proposition and the technical advantages of our products
  • You love solving technical challenges and thrive on bringing creative solutions to our customers
  • You should have a technical mindset and a desire to grow technically.
  • Must be located in Switzerland

Bonus Points For:

  • Experience with Open Source technologies, or in the Metrics/Monitoring space is an advantage
  • Experience with sales methodologies like MEDD(P)ICC is a plus

Compensation & Rewards

In Switzerland, the OTE (On-Target Earnings) compensation range for this role is CHF 206,000 - CHF 246,000. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

  • 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
  • Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
  • Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.
  • Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.
  • Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.
  • Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
  • Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
  • Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
  • Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.
  • In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.
  • Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable.

Equal Opportunity Employer: Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, nationality, origin, caste, sex, gender reassignment identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion or belief, disability, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, maternity, marital, family or carer status, or any other characteristic which is protected by local law. We believe that equality and diversity build a strong organisation, and we work hard to ensure that is the foundation of our organisation as we grow.
